doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Snare drum to full kit, and professional work instead of school music
summary: Brown asks about moving from snare to kit; Hamilton says he played no music at school, worked gigs from age 15 or 16, and out-earned his father at about $27 a week.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well I was going to say, you know, turn around. Well I want to go back because, you know, since we’re in a room full of drummers, that transition from playing a snare drum to the full kit is a significant transition, conceptually,
technique, and I’m just trying to get as much as you can tell me about your earliest experience with this instrument. And plus, in school, what kind of music are you playing in school?
Just jazz. They let you play jazz in school?
I only played in the band, marching band, one semester and I told you why, just to get my sweater, you know. In the meantime man, I’m working, I’m playing the joints.
So you’re not really playing music in school as much, you’re playing outside.

I’m not playing music in school period. I was working with groups. Fifteen, 16 years old, man, I was making gigs, and I mean big time gigs. As a matter of fact man, when I graduated from Jeff -- oh, I came back and graduated. I was 19 years old. I was making more money then my father. Man, I was making around $27, $28 a week.
Well I was going to ask you how much was Hamp paying you for the three weeks. How much was he paying you?
It was just the thrill of being in band, right?
